purpose: G4 (C2 direction 2026-10-31, own C1-motivated WAM VQ framework): do gradients of the C1 objectives on shared VQ parameters carry over to other contexts at fresh noise? fwld1 (26063678) on the per-layer rank-4 branch: future path 67% trajectory / 33% context / 0.2% generic, T(other context, seed 1) 0.021 (future) vs 0.423 (action). Q0 tuned codebooks / row gains and its held-out future fell 13-16%. Here the same Gram test on GPTVQ W2 (explicit codebooks, the closest host to Q0 and to our own representation), on three codebook sharing levels and three scale/bias families, objectives separately: Z, K and A.

host.codes: the baseline stores dense BF16 weights only: per codebook block (rows_per_group rows x 256 columns, 4-dim vectors along the input dimension, from the layer's stats config) the distinct BF16 4-vectors are the codebook entries in use (<= 256 required) and their index per vector the code

excluded: the 6 time-conditioning Linears (video/action time_embedding.0/.2, time_projection.1): they carry no future error (tcond 26066073, 0.999x) and soak up the gradient by sensitivity

families.book: per codebook entry an offset in weight units, W_v = c_(b,k) + delta_(b,k): GPTVQ's native sharing (one codebook per 131072 weights)
families.layer: per layer 256 meta-entries: the layer's codebook entries in span-normalized coordinates (entry / span max) clustered into 256 (weighted k-means, usage counts); one offset per meta-entry in normalized units, W_v = s_span (c_hat + delta_m): one codebook per layer, as Q0
families.module: the same with 256 meta-entries per module (video body, action body, other) clustered over all its layers: one codebook per module
families.row: per output row a log-scale, W_ij -> e^(r_i) W_ij
families.col: per input column a log-scale, W_ij -> W_ij e^(c_j)
families.bias: per output channel an additive output offset (zero bits once folded into the bias)

metric: each family in coordinates where the Euclidean norm is the Frobenius norm of the weight change it makes (bias: of the output change, E|x|^2/in from the grad passes): offsets divided by sqrt(usage), normalized offsets by sqrt(sum s_span^2 usage), log-scales by the row/column norm. Per tensor (a layer, or a module for 'module') a relative step -eta ref g/|g| with ref = |W| (bias: |W| sqrt(E|x|^2/in); module: sqrt(sum |W|^2)); one global normalized step reported next to it
samples: fwld1's: the 40 contexts of the first 4 loss-pair training batches x sampler seed indices 0 and 1 (seed-1 BF16 teachers from results/lowrank/diag/teachers)

paths.Z: lambda Z through the student query (cotangent at the student future)
paths.K: beta K: the frozen BF16 reader on the student future, through the student query
paths.A: A_tf: the student reading the BF16 teacher future (fwld1's A path)

checks.basis: the grad replay must reproduce the staged no-grad pass; a layer with a block of > 256 distinct vectors is not coded as configured: it keeps its plain forward, is listed in codes.json, and such layers may hold at most skipped_share_max of the target weights (r1 26071863 met one after 300 layers); per pass and layer sum_i(row grad) = sum_j(col grad) = sum_(b,k) <book grad, entry> per layer (each is sum G o W), relative to sum |G o W|

reading.primary: T_F->F(other context, seed 1) per book family: first-order decrease of the future loss (Z + K) on other contexts at fresh noise from a step along a batch's seed-0 mean future gradient, over that on the batch itself, summed over the 4 batches (fwld1's T); reference: rank-4 branch 0.021
reading.go: some book family (book, layer or module) reaches go_min: shared codebook parameters carry a C1 future correction that transfers; next, calibrate that family on the winning objective and check held-out future (<= 0.9x U)
reading.weak: best book family in [weak_min, go_min): partial transfer; retest on our own initialization at the winning sharing level before training
reading.no_go: all book families below weak_min: at W2 A16 the future side is not repairable through shared parameters either; C2 protects the future through bits only and calibrates the action side

save: results/vqg4/GPTVQ/{codes.json, samples/<case>_<seed>.pt (raw per-layer gradients, book in BF16), gram.pt, summary.json, RESULTS.zh.md}

allocation.time_basis: load ~10 min; code recovery and k-means a few min; 80 samples x (query + teacher-future read + K read with grad + 3 parameter reverse passes) ~40 s (fwld1: F + A ~25 s) ~55 min; grams ~10 min. Samples saved per file, rN resumes

race_allocation.basis: user (2026-10-31): race a > 2 h g1 job against the gdev job; the first to start stays, the other is qdel'ed; same results dir
